description: The bar chart illustrates the negative log-probabilities for clinically relevant tokens across different clinical specialties, comparing the baseline Mistral-v0.2 model with the same model fine-tuned on various specialty data. The horizontal axis represents the per-specialty terms, labeled as Cardio, Gastro, Infect, Neuro, Obstetrics, and Pediatrics, while the vertical axis is labeled "Negative log probability" with a linear scale ranging from -27 to -22, with tick labels at intervals of 1. The chart features grouped bars, with each group representing a clinical specialty and containing six bars colored according to the fine-tuning specialty data: light blue for the baseline model, and shades of orange and brown for fine-tuning on Cardio, Gastro, Infect, Neuro, Obstetrics, and Pediatrics, respectively. Within each group, the bars are arranged in the same order, representing the different fine-tuning datasets. The bar heights vary across groups and fine-tuning datasets, with the Cardio group showing the lowest negative log-probability value of approximately -26.5 for the baseline model and values ranging from around -22.5 to -23.5 for the fine-tuned models, while the other groups have values generally between -24 and -22. The bars within each group are not sorted in a specific order, but the groups are arranged in a specific order along the horizontal axis, corresponding to the different clinical specialties.
